relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a PSTPIP1 variant carrier: "Genetic testing identified a heterozygous pathogenic variant in PSTPIP1".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a script only assembled the JSON. One in-scope person (the single unnamed case-report patient, label 'patient'). Parents are mentioned only as lacking similar symptoms, not as tested or affected, so they get no rows. Previously published people in the Discussion (refs 1, 3, 8, 12) are not given individual-level detail; ref (3) is 'a case report describing PAPASH syndrome coexisting with scalp psoriasis' but the number of people is not stated, so no row was created. Inheritance left 'not reported': the authors 'suggested' de novo only from the parents' lack of symptoms, without stated parental testing (rule 8, D-24). Variant type not stated by the authors (not derived from HGVS). Ages: arthritis was 'diagnosed at age 17' (age at diagnosis of arthritis, kept in feature detail rather than as onset or PAPASH diagnosis age); acne 'since adolescence' (feature onset); 30 years old at referral in 2014; PAPASH diagnosed in 2021 at an unstated age; age at last follow-up (April 2025) not stated. Individual-level onset left 'not reported'. 'no joint symptoms' at the April 2025 follow-up is a treatment-response state, not recorded as excluded arthritis. 'Severe skin infections' after inguinal procedures recorded as a feature, but the checklist item 'recurrent infections' left not reported because recurrence is not stated. 'Normal bodyweight' recorded as excluded 'abnormal body weight' (D-27). Negative anti-adalimumab antibodies not recorded as a phenotype. Vital status 'alive' taken from the April 2025 follow-up. No contradictions found.

vital_status.span: During the latest follow-up in April 2025, the patient had been on adalimumab for over a year and reported overall stability

treatment_summary.value: Adalimumab (initially 40 mg every 2 weeks; later reintroduced at intensified dose 80 mg every 10-14 days, three introductions in total), intermittent and repeated systemic prednisolone, etanercept (ineffective), secukinumab (controlled joints, not skin), cyclosporine (exacerbated acne), ixekizumab (controlled joints, skin/PG reactivated), methotrexate (15 mg weekly early, no response, nausea; later 5 mg weekly with adalimumab), isotretinoin, acitretin, dapsone, repeated antibiotics, surgical drainage of abscesses, topical clindamycin and clobetasol.
span: he had been on adalimumab (40 mg every 2 weeks) for 1 year, along with intermittent prednisolone
A 6-month trial of etanercept (50 mg weekly) was attempted but proved ineffective, leading to its replacement with secukinumab (150–300 mg every 4 weeks)
The newly activated PG was treated with prednisolone and cyclosporine (4.3 mg/kg), but cyclosporine induced a rapid exacerbation of acne within weeks

adalimumab was reintroduced at an intensified dose (80 mg every 10–14 days), leading to rapid PG improvement and reduced HS activity. However, arthritis flares increased after 2 years, prompting a switch to ixekizumab (80 mg every 3–4 weeks)
Other agents trialled alongside biologics included isotretinoin, acitretin, and dapsone

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: Clinical suspicion of PAPASH after rheumatologic reassessment, confirmed by single-gene PSTPIP1 analysis (sequence and CNV) identifying a heterozygous pathogenic variant
span: a detailed rheumatologic reassessment and literature review raised suspicion of an autoinflammatory syndrome, such as PAPASH
single-gene analysis of PSTPIP1, including both sequence analysis and copy number variation (CNV) analysis, was performed
Genetic testing identified a heterozygous pathogenic variant in PSTPIP1: NM_003978.5:c.688G>A p.(Ala230Thr), confirming the PAPASH syndrome
